t: What Everyone Gets Wrong About Gravity
desc:
The General Theory of Relativity tells us gravity is not a force, gravitational fields don't exist. Objects tend to move on straight paths through curved spacetime. Thanks to Caséta by Lutron for sponsoring this video. Find out more at: https://www.lutron.com/veritasium

Huge thanks to Prof. Geraint Lewis for hours of consulting on this video so I could get these ideas straight in my own brain. Ch

recs.stt: Why gravity is not like the other forces
recs.x:
(This is me trying to condense what could be a 10 minute explanation into a few sentences, so apologies if it's not particularly clear.)

Veritasium had a good video on this topic: [link] (Thanks to u/badocr for commenting with this link last time.)

Ah yeah there are multiple definitions of 'acceleration' here. Unruh radiation occurs when you're not 'in an inertial reference frame,' loosely meaning that you feel acceleration. So in a rocket in space or (presumably) standing on Earth's surface.

What you say makes intuitive sense, but it was actually the opposite logic that lead Einstein to his general theory of relativity. Here's a slightly dorky but very good Veritasium video that explains this issue and general relativity [link]

cites.stt: Weightless cats – Do space cats land on their feet? (2011) [video]
cites.x: While falling, the cat is in an inertial reference frame, so it is not accelerating. The ground is actually accelerating upward at 9.8 m/s2, counteracting the flow of spacetime.
